header.running_head: Rasulullaah ﷺ Endures Hardship and Difficulty when Giving Da'wah towards Allaah

blocks.text: Rasulullaah ﷺ up so badly that he fell unconscious. Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then said, "Shame on you people! Will you kill a man for saying, 'Allaah is my Rabb'?" When someone asked who he was, the others replied, "He is the madman Abu Bakr."[^1] Another narration[^2] states that at this juncture, the people left Rasulullaah ﷺ and attacked Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA).
The Comment of Hadhrat Ali (RA) Concerning the Courage of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) to Deliver a Sermon

While addressing the people, Hadhrat Ali (RA) once asked, "O people! Who is the most courageous person?" "You are, O Ameerul Mu'mineen," the people submitted. Hadhrat Ali (RA) then said, "Although I have defeated everyone who has confronted me, the most courageous person is Abu Bakr (RA). We had constructed a shed for Rasulullaah ﷺ (during the Battle of Badr) and then asked who would remain with Rasulullaah ﷺ so that the Mushrikeen do not attack him. By Allaah! Whenever a Mushrik even drew close to us Abu Bakr (RA) was there with his sword drawn near the head side of Rasulullaah ﷺ. He attacked anyone who dared attack Rasulullaah ﷺ. He was certainly the bravest of people."

Hadhrat Ali (RA) continues, "I have seen the Quraysh grab hold of Rasulullaah ﷺ with one person treating him angrily and another shaking him while they said to him, 'Do you make all the gods into one?!' By Allaah! None of us dared go close to Rasulullaah ﷺ (for fear of being beaten) besides Abu Bakr (RA). He would hit one person, wrestle with another and shake someone else as he said, 'Shame on you people! Will you kill a man for saying, 'Allaah is my Rabb'?'"

Hadhrat Ali (RA) then lifted the shawl he was wearing and wept until his beard became wet. He then said, "I ask you to swear by Allaah whether the Mu'min[^3] from the court of Fir'oun was better or Abu Bakr (RA)." When everyone remained silent, Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "By Allaah! A moment of the life of Abu Bakr (RA) is better than the earth full of people like the Mu'min from the court of Fir'oun. While the Mu'min from the court of Fir'oun concealed his Imaan, Abu Bakr (RA) made his Imaan public."[^4]
